hoeflin.ada.command_line: OS argument strings/counts and Ada Value parsing/failure behavior remain unproved; modeled observations cover typed normal-return options and, where recognized, the restricted decimal grammar.
hoeflin.ada.numerics.long_elementary_functions: Installed elementary-function specifications are trusted interfaces. Their implementations, analytic accuracy, rounding/error bounds and totality are not proved; Ghost acceptance predicates model checked normal returns.
hoeflin.ada.text_io: Text_IO and its instantiated numeric formatting generics, buffering, physical stdout/file bytes, persistence and exceptions remain unproved. Ghost models cover nominal fields/layouts and input/output observations only.
hoeflin.interfaces: Machine integer representation and runtime/compiler implementation of interface operations remain trusted; project arithmetic proofs concern Ada semantics, not generated machine-code verification.
hoeflin.interfaces.c: C double conversion, foreign ABI, libm implementation, error behavior and platform representation remain trusted; the C erfc boundary is explicitly modeled but not proved.

towers.ada.command_line: OS argument strings/counts and Ada Value parsing/failure behavior remain unproved; modeled observations cover typed normal-return options and, where recognized, the restricted decimal grammar.
towers.ada.directories: Directory creation, permissions, filesystem persistence and failure behavior remain unproved; a Ghost report request or normal return is not a proof of physical files.
towers.ada.numerics: The Pi constant and runtime numeric definitions are trusted target representations, not derived exact-real constants or validation of a Gaussian model.
towers.ada.numerics.long_elementary_functions: Installed elementary-function specifications are trusted interfaces. Their implementations, analytic accuracy, rounding/error bounds and totality are not proved; Ghost acceptance predicates model checked normal returns.
towers.ada.strings.fixed: The standard trimming implementation and exception behavior are unproved; Ghost lexical observations do not verify the trimming backend.
towers.ada.text_io: Text_IO and its instantiated numeric formatting generics, buffering, physical stdout/file bytes, persistence and exceptions remain unproved. Ghost models cover nominal fields/layouts and input/output observations only.
towers.interfaces.c: C double conversion, foreign ABI, libm implementation, error behavior and platform representation remain trusted; the C erfc boundary is explicitly modeled but not proved.

global_unproved_obligations.numerical-backends: C erfc, Ada elementary-function implementations, ABI/representation, rounding accuracy and backend totality are unproved. Ghost predicates describe checked normal-return properties, not certified analytic functions or error bounds.
global_unproved_obligations.runtime-and-io: Ada runtime, argument retrieval/Value attributes, string/image/formatting generics, memory/resource failures, filesystem effects, permissions, buffering, physical bytes, and exception/failure semantics remain unproved. Ghost ledgers record observations/requests and normal returns, not operating-system success or full persistent output traces.
global_unproved_obligations.model-adequacy: An analyzed Ghost model does not prove that an excluded implementation refines it, that guards never reject, or that the model is a complete specification. Decimal recognition, lexical fields, bounded payload summaries and nominal layouts have stated restricted scopes; coupled calls in Off bodies are execution observations, not static refinement proofs.
global_unproved_obligations.psychometric-validity: No Ghost model establishes empirical test correlations, population calibration, Gaussian distributions, pseudo-random independence, extreme-tail frequencies, reliability interpretation or psychometric validity. These require separate mathematical/statistical and empirical justification.
global_unproved_obligations.toolchain-and-provers: Compiler/runtime translation, target floating representation, GNATprove/Why3/SMT solvers, operating system and hardware are trusted verification infrastructure; neither their implementations nor independent proof-object checking are proved by this campaign.
